quest.title: Qimen Arts and the Rite of Homa, the Spirits are Calmed and Life Restored
quest.description: After two days have passed, you decide to visit the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor to see if Hu Tao has returned...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x30, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6, Unknown Item #363372 x1

chapter.title: Qimen Arts and the Rite of Homa, the Spirits are Calmed and Life Restored

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: #Hmm? {NICKNAME}, Paimon. How are you feeling after your trip to the border?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're feeling great, thanks! We just heard you were taking part in this Seven-and-Eight-Gates Method, so we came to see if there were any issues.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Gate of Terrain...

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: No need to worry. Though the Gate of Terrain symbolizes fire and volatility, it also stands for light, growth, and prosperity. For that reason, it is seen as a somewhat auspicious gate.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: The greatest challenge of tonight will be found not here, but at Hu Tao's Gate of Death.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: I will do my utmost to alleviate her burden.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, everyone's here already...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Hey, Paimon. Did you have a good rest?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, yup! Pretty good, thanks!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How's the situation looking?

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Since we last met, we've seen an uptick in patient numbers in Liyue Harbor.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Also, my cousin wrote back to me. She mentioned that people have started to get sick in Yilong Wharf as well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no, it's spread to Yilong Wharf now?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Mm, but as long as we solve the core problem, the fetor in people's bodies will dissipate, and they'll make a speedy recovery.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: And the good news is that thanks to the Tianquan's efforts, we now have the locations of all eight gates.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Woohoo! So what's the plan?

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Tonight, we will deploy the array, and set up a Homa Altar at each of the gates. This will enable the funeral parlor's secret art to incinerate the fetor.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Since the gates are interconnected via the Ley Lines, the secret art will be amplified to all of Liyue. Not a single wisp of fetor will escape its grasp.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm! It's gonna be the biggest purification ceremony in the funeral parlor's history.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Okay, so what are the locations of the eight gates?

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: You needn't worry — they're all accounted for. Actually, we already knew the locations of the first four two days ago.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Keqing has already set out for the Gate of Life in Yilong Wharf, and Ganyu is en route to the Gate of Concealment at Mt. Aocang. Beidou is covering the Gate of Fright at Guyun Stone Forest, and Yelan will tackle the Gate of Injury at The Chasm.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: As of last night, we confirmed the locations of the remaining four gates. The fifth is the Gate of Terrain at Dihua Marsh, which the Conqueror of Demons has pledged to defend.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: The sixth is the Gate of Repose in Qingce Village. This one has been claimed by the Bubu Pharmacy duo.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: The seventh is the Gate of Initiation, located here in Liyue Harbor. Lan Yan and I will see to this one.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What about the final gate?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Last but not least is the Gate of Death at Wuwang Hill. Which, let's be honest, has Director Hu written all over it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Wait, so you've assigned all of the gates already!?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Sorry! You got here too late.

choices.text: Let me take the Gate of Death.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: You trying to steal my job now? Nuh-uh, hands off!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But the Gate of Death sounds so dangerous... And you only just got back from the border...

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: You're right that it's the most dangerous gate. Which is exactly why it needs an expert on life and death like me!

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: If you have to take a gate, go steal the Tianquan's instead, hehe.

response.speaker: Ningguang
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, I appreciate your eagerness to help, and as it happens, Miss Lan Yan and I do have a matter we'd like to discuss with you.

response.speaker: Lan Yan
response.text: That's right. But let's discuss it once Director Hu's done with you.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wait... so Director Hu DOES need me for something?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Hehe, sorry, I went ahead and told them I'd be stealing you for a little while.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: I haven't had much time to enjoy myself this Lantern Rite. And come this evening, I have to leave the city again, which means I'll miss out on all the lanterns.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: So I want to use the little down time I have to go hand out some fortune coins to my friends. Then I can at least say I did Lantern Rite this year. Fancy joining me for that?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Absolutely.

response.speaker: Ningguang
response.text: Hehe, this is the one thing Director Hu's had to look forward to. Otherwise, she'd have set out for Wuwang Hill by now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, so you were waiting for us all this time?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Hehe, it's okay. Since time was tight, I already asked the Tianquan to pass along my fortune coins to all the people handling the gates.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: I'm grateful for their help — it should have been the funeral parlor's responsibility, after all.

response.speaker: Ningguang
response.text: Think nothing of it, Director Hu.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Anyway, I have a few friends left to visit in Liyue Harbor. Let's do the rounds, shall we?

choices.text: Alright, lemme guess: There's a secret ninth gate for me?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! People are always saying eight gates when they mean nine — it happens all the time, right?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Nope, not in my experience.

talks.objective: Go with Hu Tao to meet your friends

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: #Hu Tao, {NICKNAME}, and Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Oh? I didn't expect to see you here at this hour.

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: We are just about to set out for Qingce Village!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Hehe, guess we caught you just in time, then. We're here to deliver some fortune coins!

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Hm, you're in unusually good spirits, Director Hu... Even pesky Baizhu gets a fortune coin today?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Of course, of course! There's enough for everyone. Here, this one's for you.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: It's the sun symbol...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: You're absolutely right, Dr. Baizhu — in terms of your peskiness, I mean.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: So I'm afraid I won't be wishing you success in your medical and immortality-seeking endeavors. That would just make things unnecessarily difficult for me.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: The sun symbol symbolizes peace and harmony in the world. My wish is that all shall be cured of their ailments before arriving at your door, so you'll be spared the sight of pain and suffering.

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: Haha, I see. Director Hu's hoping that you go out of business, Baizhu.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Hehe, Changsheng, this one's for you.

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: Let me see, let me see... Ooh, a cross symbol!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm! The cross symbol represents growth, prosperity, and balance between heaven and earth. May you soon regain all the power and memories you possessed in your prime!

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: That's very thoughtful of you, Director Hu. I assume you also brought one for Qiqi?

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: F—For me?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Yup! This peace symbol coin is for you, Qiqi. It symbolizes safe passage. In other words — stay away from dangerous places the next time you go herb-gathering.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: If anything were to happen to you, poor Mr. Baizhu would be in a real pickle — because he'd have no one to study the secrets of immortality from.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: And I'd be affected too, of course. I can't bury you if I don't know where you are.

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Uh, got it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw, it's nice to see that Qiqi's recovering well from all that fetor at the border.

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: I am a zombie. Zombies can't get sick.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: In fact, Qiqi insisted on joining me at the gate tonight. She's determined to help eradicate the fetor.

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Bad fetor. I don't like it.

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: It can make people sick, and then Baizhu has to heal them. It can also make people die. And then they have to get buried by Hu Tao.

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Too much trouble...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Don't worry, Qiqi. Tonight, we'll solve the problem once and for all.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Alright, everyone, we won't overstay our welcome.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: One moment, Director Hu.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: What's wrong? ...Huh? Wait, what are you doing?

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: Aha, so the secret art works even when there's no illness present... Seems like a sizeable step forward for Baizhu's research.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Tonight, you will stand guard over the Gate of Death — the most ominous gate of them all. It may not help much, but I transferred a little extra life force to you. May it help you stay alert and focused during the proceedings.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Hopefully not at a detriment to your own health, though?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: You needn't worry about that. As your archenemy, why would I undermine myself to help my opponent?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Hahaha, alright, well said. Okay — this time I really am leaving. Bye, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Good luck, Hu Tao...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Oh, Yun Jin! Aka, Ms. Yun! Also aka Director Yun!

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: #Huh? Hu Tao? What brings you here? Oh, and {NICKNAME} and Paimon, too...

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Is this about the other day? I swear, I didn't say anything bad about you! They were just trying to find out where you'd gone!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Haha, no it's not about that! I'm just here to say hi to my friend... assuming that's alright with you?

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Oh. Uh, yeah, of course!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Also, she brought some fortune coins for you!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Yep yep! Hehe, take a look!

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: What are these?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: They're fortune coins engraved with the yardstick symbol. One for you, and one for Xinyan.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: You're the top performing artists in all of Liyue Harbor, and I wish you success beyond measure!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Could you pass Xinyan's coin to her for me? I haven't been able to find her all day, but I know she won't miss your show tonight.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Thanks, Hu Tao. I really appreciate the coin! But... how come you can't just give it to her yourself this evening?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: I'd love to, but unfortunately I won't make it to the lantern display tonight. That's the whole reason I'm here now.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Oh... how come? You have something else on?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Just a little thing I have to do for work.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Ah, right... I heard the Ministry of Civil Affairs announced that they'll be reviving an ancient ceremony tonight — something about lighting a flame to dispel the smog.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Your little work thing wouldn't have anything to do with that, would it?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: You're a sharp one, Yun Jin. Yes, that's exactly it.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Is it... dangerous?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: #Technically, but only a teeny tiny little bit. {NICKNAME} will back me up on that.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah, Hu Tao's right.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: ...Are you sure?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: #Ah, come on Yun Jin. I get that you won't take my word for it, but if you can't trust {NICKNAME}, whom can you trust?

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: I didn't mean it like that... Anyway, since you can't make it tonight, how about I sing "The Sanctification of Tao Dou" for you right now? Does that sound good?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Hehe, that's so nice of you! But since you're offering... I'd rather hear a certain other tune instead. You know the one, right?

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Uh... which one? Sorry, I'm a little lost...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: You know! You've sung it to me before!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What are you talking about? Is this supposed to be a riddle?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: The opera version of the Hilitune! We made a bet, and agreed that whoever lost had to sing lyrics chosen by the winner in their own style. The result was Yun Jin's spectacular operatic version of the Hilitune. You guys seriously need to hear it.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: #Aw, Yun Jin... Don't tell me you're embarrassed to sing it now that {NICKNAME} is here...?

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: What are you talking about? Of course not...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Pretty please, Yun Jin? Just once, for me? I really want to hear it again.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Alright, alright, I'll sing it for you after the show tonight. How about that?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Noooooo, I want to hear it now!

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Why?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Oh, don't play dumb, you know why! Hu Tao's a sassy little brat who always gets whatever she wants! Mostly because she's sooo adorable that no one has the heart to turn her down! La-la-la-la-la, life is grand~

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: *sigh* You are unbelievable... Alright. I'll sing, but please — do not laugh at me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yay! Operatic Hilitune, let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: ♪ Silly-churl, billy-churl, silly-billy Hilichurl... ♪

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Bravo, bravissimo! Well, what do you think — glad I dragged you out now?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It was a truly unique performance.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: I must look ridiculous...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Hee-hee, thanks for indulging me, Yun Jin. You're a star! We should head off now, as I still have one person to give a fortune coin to.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: No, wait... Hu Tao, be honest. You guys aren't hiding anything from me, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Of course not! Put that thought right out of your head.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Alright. Then whenever you're done with your work — whether it's tomorrow, the day after, or whenever — come find me again, and I'll sing "The Sanctification of Tao Dou" for you.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: ...Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: #Let me rephrase. Hu Tao, {NICKNAME} — promise me you'll come and see me perform some day soon, okay?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Sure! You got it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! You got a new outfit too? You look amazing, Xiangling!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Ooh, you think? Hmm, then what does that say about my taste? Hint, hint?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Yeah, yeah, Director Hu has the most exquisite taste in the world, et cetera.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I see, so it's a gift from Hu Tao.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: A thank-you gift, technically. I sought out that Fontaine fashion designer and gave her a brief description of Xiangling.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Her work is incredible! Especially this Guoba hat. It's just as cute as the real Guoba!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's great seeing both of you together dressed in your new outfits. You almost look like sisters!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Hehe, that's a given!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Oh, also — Xiangling, I got you a little something else too. It's a fortune coin.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: This career fortune coin is for you! May you go from strength to strength, and may the Wanmin Restaurant get so many customers that it needs to be rebuilt ten times bigger!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: I dunno, Hu Tao, you're kind of asking a lot of me there...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Wait, I'm not done! I've got two more coins — a "family fortune" one for Xingqiu, and a "spirit and vigor" one for Chongyun. I believe they've already left for Chenyu Vale, so could you pass them on when they get back?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Uh... Why get me involved? Can't you just give these to them yourself?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Ugh, because I've gotta work tonight. And I don't wanna keep them waiting.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Fair enough... Wait, does that mean you're involved in tonight's ceremony thing? I heard the announcement from the Ministry of Civil Affairs.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: That's the one! As soon as the ceremony is complete, Xingqiu's great-grandfather will start to recover, and Miss Ying'er's boyfriend will be as right as rain.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Whoa, sounds amazing! So is this what's been keeping you busy these past few days? No wonder we still haven't had that meal together... I bet you've barely had a moment to breathe.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Once the ceremony's over, come for food with us, okay?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Sure thing! Sounds good!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Promise you won't stand us up this time?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: #I promise! {NICKNAME} will hold me to it!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: #Okay, I can get behind that... If you're a no-show, I'm sending {NICKNAME} to track you down and drag you back to the dinner table kicking and screaming!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Mission accepted.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Great, then we have a deal! We should head out now — see you later Xiangling!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hee-hee, Paimon's so excited! What fortune are we gonna get?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Give me a second... Aha, found it! Here's yours, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What does this symbol mean?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: It's a treasure symbol! My wish for you is that you'll always have an endless supply of Mora, so you can eat whatever you want, whenever you want!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! You get Paimon like no one else does... Thank you, Hu Tao! Thank you so, so much!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So where's mine, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I haven't forgotten you! Just give me a moment, I'll be right back.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Hu Tao enters the funeral parlor. Before long, she comes skipping back out in her old outfit.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Why'd you change back, Hu Tao?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Because I'll be working tonight! Hehe, I've always been very serious when it comes to work.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Is this my gift?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Look again! Do you see anything about me that's different from before?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Heh... I mean, yes, but I was hoping you'd be a little more observant than that...

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Here. This plum branch is for you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, isn't this the branch from your hat!?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: #Yes, and going back further, it's from a tree that I planted myself. {NICKNAME}, you have countless friends in Liyue Harbor, so I'm sure you'll get plenty of fortune coins.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: I wanted to give you something different. Something that will remind you of me whenever you look at it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eek! Paimon doesn't like the sound of that!

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Okay, then I'll rephrase: Something you can take a look at whenever you miss me.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You just made it worse!

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: What do you mean? I don't know what's going through your head... Look, all I'm saying is, I can't be by your side 24/7 like Paimon can. There's gonna be times when we're apart.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Phew, you scared Paimon!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...I've got a gift for you, too.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Huh? Wait, that sigil... Is this one of the fabled Rex coins!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You've got a great eye, Hu Tao! It's a Rex coin — although, probably not the genuine article, 'cause the Conqueror of Demons told us he couldn't sense Rex Lapis's power in it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But still, the owner before us was someone pretty important.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, that too! So maybe it can keep you safe.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Wow, this is a really special gift... I'll take it! Hehe, thank you both. I'll stay safe, don't you worry.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Anyway, it's getting late, and I have a few things to get ready before I head out to Wuwang Hill. Besides, you should probably get back to Yujing Terrace now — I know the Tianquan's still waiting for you.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Please, be careful.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Don't worry, I got this.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright then, bye-bye! And remember — the sooner you get back, the sooner we can go for a meal together! And hear Yun Jin's singing!

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Got it! See ya!

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: It was so nice to spend this time with you...

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Oh! What brings you here? No tea drinking today?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: It would be unbecoming of me to sip tea in leisure while my employer toils alone.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Aha, so you do have a heart after all.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Have you made up your mind, Director?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Throughout our history, we've fought off many existential threats with whatever tools we had at our disposal. Today is no different, we just have to rise to the challenge.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: It'll be my first time using this array, so who knows how it'll go. But if I know one thing, it's that I must drive death back where it came from.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: #Oh, also, {NICKNAME} gave me a special fortune coin — apparently, it's one of those Rex coins. You're more knowledgeable about this kind of thing than me though. So I'd appreciate your second opinion.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: It is indeed a Rex coin. It symbolizes good fortune, and may offer some use as a protective charm.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: #Got it. In that case... after tonight, could you please return it to {NICKNAME} for me?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: You wish to return the gift? For what reason?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: #{NICKNAME} reached Natlan, and took a trip to the land of the dead while there. It must have been incredibly dangerous.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: #{M#He}{F#She}'s made it this far unscathed, so clearly {F#s}he's blessed with good fortune. But {M#his}{F#her} journey will only get more dangerous with each step, and that worries me.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: #So, if there's a chance this Rex coin really can keep a person safe, I want to make sure that person is {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: #You make good points, Director. But have you considered that {NICKNAME} perhaps had similar wishes for you?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: That's another reason I can't afford to keep it...

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: #I don't know what's going to happen tonight. If worse comes to worst and I don't make it back, I don't want {NICKNAME} to find out this coin didn't work by discovering it in a pile of debris...

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: #What if it upsets {M#him}{F#her}? What if {F#s}he feels like it's all {M#his}{F#her} fault? I couldn't bear to see {M#him}{F#her} like that... You know what I mean, right, Zhongli?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: I fear that I do...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Your concern is that the sight of this coin will only make it more difficult to let go of your worldly attachments.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Haha, it's like you're a mind-reader... You know as well as I do that being too attached is a fatal flaw for a funeral director. It's a vice that's all too easy to fall prey to...

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: But this time, I must not repeat my dad's mistake. That is what's most important here.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: ...Alright, since we're this far in, I might as well just tell you the rest too. If I don't return tonight, you'll no longer be a consultant... Because you'll be the 78th Director of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: ...Your work is far from done, Director. I fear there is no one who could hope to take your place.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: "Live in life, and die in death." If my time has come, then so be it. There's no sense resisting the inevitable.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Nevertheless, I would urge caution. Focus on the task at hand, not what transpired in the past. And do not forget the rest of that saying: "Follow your heart, and do what you can."

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: I understand... Alright, it's almost time. I should get going.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: It's a really beautiful day today... I should write a poem to capture this moment.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: A butterfly dances in a crimson bouquet, for fear of the ominous rainfall that may soon show its face.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: With one last, lingering glance at that carmine hue, she lies among the petals in the garden of eternal rest, as she sets the floral incense ablaze.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: ...The lone butterfly left, but not without a trace. A fragrance remained, her butterfly's embrace.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Haha, yes! Very observant of you! And all the proof I need that you spend your free time staring longingly at pictures of me. There's no way you'd spot a detail like that otherwise.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ningguang, Lan Yan, we're back! So, what did you want to discuss?

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: I'll let Miss Lan explain.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Remember how I wrote a letter back home to ask about the array? Well, I got a reply.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Paimon remembers. So was Hu Tao right? No one has to be sacrificed, right?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: ...Unfortunately, my cousin could not give me a definitive answer on this, despite scouring the family library.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: But, given that the array gets its power from the Ley Lines, she suspects that the obfuscation requirement may be a rule laid down by the mountains and the land.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What does that mean?

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Basically... it looks likely that the obfuscation of one person is mandatory after all, because we can't violate the laws of the Ley Lines. Furthermore, the Gate of Death will be used to suppress the fetor this time... which is Director Hu's gate.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, you're saying, Hu Tao has to die!?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: If my cousin's right, and as I said, she can only speculate... But she also provided me with a method that might just be able to save Director Hu's life.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: See this? It's a rattan figure I made for the director. One of many. In case you've forgotten, they work by absorbing evil energy in their owner's place, so they won't come to harm.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: With the technique my cousin explained, I managed to connect several of these rattan figures to the gate array. That way, the fetor blast will be shared evenly by everyone in the array.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Everyone has agreed to the plan. Keqing, Ganyu, the Conqueror of Demons, Qiqi, Beidou, Yelan, Lan Yan, and I will each hold a rattan figure.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Today's Liyue draws its strength from unity. That is how we quelled an ancient god's wrath without the help of Rex Lapis, and that is why we cannot let the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor shoulder the present crisis alone.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Nevertheless, the danger posed by the fetor is not to be underestimated. The consequences could be grave, even with everyone sharing the blast.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: We would like to request your assistance, but the choice is entirely yours. If you have any reservations, we will by no means—

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Count me in.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: #What did I tell you? I knew {NICKNAME} would help us!

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Hehe, I never doubted that for a second.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Then, please take this rattan figure. I'll link you up to the array right now.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Huh? What's going on? This doesn't make any sense...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: #I... I don't think I made a mistake, but it seems like... I can't connect {NICKNAME} to the array.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: How can this be? What's the problem?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: #This should work in the exact same way as the gate array — by using the power of the Ley Lines. But the Ley Lines aren't responding to {NICKNAME}, almost as if they believe {F#s}he doesn't exist...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! So could... that be the reason?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's true that the Ley Lines do not contain any information about me.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Is that so? Then perhaps this is simply the will of fate...

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: I've never heard of anything like that before!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Can we find some other way?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: I don't know, this is the first time I've run into a situation like this... I would write to my cousin, but I think we're out of time...

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Yes... The lantern display will begin soon.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: #I know this is frustrating, but given the situation, we have no choice but to release {NICKNAME} from this duty.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: We must hope that we will be able to share the burden on Director Hu's shoulders... and we must have faith that she will return triumphant.

talks.objective: Wait for the Lantern Rite to begin...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After leaving Yujing Terrace, you spend some time staring at the Hu Tao rattan figure in your hands in dejected silence.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Before you know it, you've ended up in front of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor again.

dialogues.speaker: Yanfei
dialogues.text: Hurry! The Lantern Rite celebrations are about to begin! You don't want to miss Ms. Yun's opening show!

dialogues.speaker: Yaoyao
dialogues.text: Slow down, Yanfei! Otherwise, you're going to fall!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: There are so many people... I hope everything goes smoothly on Hu Tao's end, so she can get back here and celebrate with us soon.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Xinyan, over here! Hu Tao asked me to give you this fortune coin.

dialogues.speaker: Xinyan
dialogues.text: Wow, she got this for me? So... where did she go?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Lady Tianquan, the Gate of Initiation is now ready. We are good to go.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Thank you. It won't be long now...

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Director Hu... Good luck to us both.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon. Happy Lantern Rite.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Zhongli! How did we not think of asking Zhongli earlier...?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Regarding the Ley Lines, you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah...? How did you know that, though?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Hehe, in fact, I have been waiting here for some time now.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Zhongli, can you connect me to the Ley Lines?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: #Since the issue lies with {NICKNAME}'s unique constitution, I am afraid that I will be of no help there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Drat, Paimon totally thought you'd have the answer... Then, why were you waiting for us?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: #The Director asked me to return this Rex coin to {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: It's a gesture of goodwill from the Director. She wishes your safe passage in your future travels.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? But... what about her?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: I suppose that will be up to her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's not good enough! Surely there's gotta be something we can do?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: As it happens, there is one thing that comes to mind. Namely... If the Seven-and-Eight-Gates Method operates according to the principles of the Ley Lines, the same must also be true of the obfuscation process.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: But since you cannot connect to the Ley Lines in the first place... Do you see what that implies?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: If I can't connect to the Ley Lines... Hmm, what does that imply?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: The Lantern Rite is about to begin.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: My dear compatriots...

dialogues.speaker: Little Meng
dialogues.text: Look, it's Lady Ningguang!

dialogues.speaker: Little Fei
dialogues.text: Wow, I didn't know she was hosting it herself this year!

dialogues.speaker: Little Lulu
dialogues.text: It must be 'cause of the ceremony, right? The Ministry of Civil Affairs sent out a notice saying that this year, they're doing a whole ceremony when they light up the Mingxiao Lantern.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: ...As we stand beneath this lantern-lit night sky, I would like to pay tribute to the ways of our forebears. We pray for the cleansing fire that exorcises evil... and for peace to prevail in our nation.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Let the ceremony begin!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: D—Did it work?

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: I believe it was a success, but...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's wrong? You two look like you've seen a ghost...

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Director Hu's rattan figure has... broken. I can't sense her presence anymore...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!? How is that possible... You mean, Hu Tao's... she's... Aah, what are we gonna do!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hmm? Where'd {NICKNAME} go?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: #It would seem that {F#s}he had something of a breakthrough. So, I sent {F#her on her}{M#him on his} way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A breakthrough? About what?

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: Hey there you two... I wasn't expecting your company here at Mt. Aocang.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We heard you were taking part in this Seven-and-Eight-Gates Method, so we came to see how you were doing.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Gate of Concealment...

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: Don't worry. This Gate is a place of refuge, peace, and good fortune. It's the perfect place for Master and the other adepti to live in seclusion. I believe they're currently discussing something in Master's abode.

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: Once this crisis is over, you'd be more than welcome to come and stay here for a little while. It'd be good for your health.

talks.objective: Find Hu Tao as soon as possible

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (If I can't connect to the Ley Lines, I can't be obfuscated by them either.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (That means I can take Hu Tao's place in the array and no one has to get sacrificed. As long as I can find her, that is...)

talks.objective: Follow the rattan figure to search for Hu Tao

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: #Oh, {NICKNAME}, Paimon... What brings you here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We heard you were taking part in this Seven-and-Eight-Gates Method, so we came to see how you were doing.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: I see. So Ningguang's explained the situation to you already.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Gate of Life...

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: The Gate of Life symbolizes growth, prosperity, and revitalization. It is the most auspicious of all eight gates. As you can see, this gate is currently situated at Yilong Wharf.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Later tonight, I will use the power of this gate and Director Hu's rattan figure to take on some of the fetor blast for her. With each gate helping to share the load... Yes, I'm sure we'll make it through this crisis.

talks.objective: Find Hu Tao as soon as possible

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (She's not here... But these are her things...)

response.speaker: Staff of Homa
response.text: (The flaming staff lies quietly on the ground, as if aware that its owner has left the world.)

response.speaker: Homa Altar
response.text: (The fire in the altar has almost gone out. But some stray sparks flicker and frolic within the ashes... in true Hu Tao fashion.)

response.speaker: Rattan Figure
response.text: (Do you remember who the rattan figure was made for? I'm sure you do.)

response.speaker: Tree Shaped Like "Tao Dou"
response.text: (That crooked tree at the center of the border looks just like this year's Mingxiao lantern. There are some cracks in the middle of the trunk... they seem to lead to somewhere far away.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Examine the fissures)

response.speaker: Tree Shaped Like "Tao Dou"
response.text: (Something just flew out of your backpack...)

talks.objective: Find Hu Tao as soon as possible

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Good luck. I'll be waiting for you.

talks.objective: Cross over to the other side, towards the next life...

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Hey! How'd you end up stranded out here? Ningguang didn't actually rope you into this too, did she?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We heard you were taking part in this Seven-and-Eight-Gates Method, so we came to see how it's going.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Gate of Fright...

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Ah, so you already know what's what.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Since ancient times, the Gate of Fright has been known as a gate of great misfortune. It usually shows up in places filled with fear and desolation.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: I guess this place checks all the boxes, with all the demons Rex Lapis suppressed here.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: But the Crux Fleet is right at home in places like this, hahaha.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: If I didn't have to work tonight, I'd have loved to take you on a walk around the area.

talks.objective: Cross over to the other side, towards the next life...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Grandpa... and Dad. Are you here to take me to the other side?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: How'd I do as director, huh? Did I do the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor proud?

dialogues.speaker: Father
dialogues.text: Absolutely. You did a million times better than me.

dialogues.speaker: Grandfather
dialogues.text: Our little girl is the best.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Good. Then... I can join you with no regrets...

dialogues.speaker: Father
dialogues.text: We're proud of you, little lady. But we only came to see you because we've missed you.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: I've missed you, too... But are you saying... you're not here to bring me into the afterlife?

dialogues.speaker: Grandfather
dialogues.text: Live in life, and die in death.... My child, your time has not yet come.

dialogues.speaker: Father
dialogues.text: Yes... The day of reunion will come in good time. There is no need to rush.

dialogues.speaker: Grandfather
dialogues.text: Look. Someone's here to take you home.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You wake up two days later in the back room of Bubu Pharmacy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're finally awake! How do you feel? Does anything hurt?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What happened...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You've been asleep for two whole days! If Baizhu hadn't insisted that you were just out from exhaustion, Paimon would've been worried sick!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still, it is a relief to see you finally wake up again. Guess Baizhu knew what he was talking about.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: When did I get here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The night of Lantern Rite, of course! Hu Tao carried you here on her back. Paimon was so worried to see you unconscious... Thankfully, Zhongli was there too, and he said you'd be fine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That being said... Why did you sneak off without saying a word? Were you trying to beat Hu Tao's record for running away and getting stranded in the border?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It was an emergency.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, yeah, Paimon knows. Hu Tao told us the whole story. Sounds like you did something pretty amazing!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You've had a lot of visitors over the last couple of days. Zhongli, Ningguang, Lan Yan... and pretty much everyone else you could think of!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are they still here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Most of them have probably left by now, but Hu Tao's still waiting out in the main room. She's been there the whole time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Anyway, you stay in bed and get some rest! Paimon will go get Baizhu to take a look at you.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As you walk out of Bubu Pharmacy's back room, you are greeted by the peaceful and festive view of Liyue Harbor. A sense of relief washes over you.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Just then, you feel something cool against your face... You've been ambushed again.
One more time, guess whooo~?

choices.text: I recognize those dulcet tones anywhere, Zhongli.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Good! If you have the energy to joke around, it means you're making a good recovery!

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: I'm so glad! Looks like I can stop worrying now... Welcome back, my hero!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You are the real hero.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Hahaha, don't be silly. It's just the two of us here, you really want to talk in glib pleasantries? 'Cause I can out-glib you any day of the week if that's how you wanna do this.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Alright, um... So, how are you holding up?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: I'm doing great, thanks to a certain someone! Baizhu gave me a checkup too.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: You look remarkably well too, considering what you went through. But are you sure you're well enough to leave yet? You'll only make things worse if you power through before you've fully healed.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'll be fine.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Well, I sure hope so... You know, I was really surprised you came to rescue me. You took such a huge risk... When did you become so reckless?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I learned from the best, Director Hu...

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Hmph... Hey, look! Liyue Harbor looks so pretty from this angle... Let's see, what's everyone doing at this hour?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Hmm... Those two kids look like they're in a hurry... I bet they're racing each other to the fortune coins.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: And that lady over there — her cheeks are so red, you'd think she's caught the sun... Aha, yes! She must be waiting for her lover so they can go set off some fireworks together!

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Such a marvelous view. Really puts me in a poetic mood! Hee-hee, okay, I got something:

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: As fresh festivities fill the streets, while lanterns light the sky like countless times before...

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: I dwell not on the twists and turns of bygone years, but remember this: that with each new day, I receive the gift of life once more.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: #Thank you, {NICKNAME}. Happy Lantern Rite.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Good! You still recognize me. So the fetor didn't fry your brain.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Oh? Fancy seeing you here. Don't you have business with Director Hu to attend to?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, you really gather intel like it's going out of fashion... But anyway — we heard you were taking part in this Seven-and-Eight-Gates Method, so we came to check-in.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Gate of Injury...

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: It's piqued your curiosity, huh? Well, this is one of the least fun gates there is. The Gate of Injury symbolizes wounds and loss. It's one of the three gates of great misfortune, along with the Gates of Death and Fright.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: A long, long time ago, this was actually the home of the present-day people of Chenyu Vale.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: But as you know, there was a huge disaster here. My ancestors fought alongside the Yakshas, and gave their lives to save Liyue from peril.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: That's why it has to be me here, guarding this gate. Unless you've got other burning questions, I must ask you to leave at once.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: I'm sure you still remember the time we explored the depths of this place together... And I trust you haven't forgotten just how dangerous it was?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: We are grateful for Director Hu's well wishes. Don't worry about us — focus on your own duties.

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Good luck, Hu Tao...

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Hope everything goes smoothly. And don't leave me hanging this time!

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: #See you shortly, {NICKNAME}. We'll be waiting!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the eight gates...

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Oh? You want to learn more about the gates? Well, as you heard earlier, the gates are basically eight key nodes in Liyue's Ley Line network.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: You must be wondering why the Ministry of Civil Affairs had to do so much work to find out the locations of the gates?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Well, the Qimen arts teach that the state of the Ley Lines is intricately linked to human activity. Each can affect the other.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: In other words, the gates' locations are subject to change over time.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: For instance, before our ancestors moved to Chenyu Vale, they lived near the Chasm. My grandpa says that back then, the gate there was the Gate of Life — yet all these years on, it's become the Gate of Injury.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: So we had to map out the gates all over again to make sure we're deploying the array properly.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Don't forget to come back here after Director Hu is done with you. There's a favor I would like to ask of you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the people assigned to the eight gates...

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Heh, you want to drop by and say hello to them? Well, you'd better hurry if you want to make it back in time.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: The Gate of Life is at Yilong Wharf, and the Gate of Concealment at Mt. Aocang. They are being seen to by Keqing and Ganyu respectively.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: The Gate of Fright can be found at Guyun Stone Forest, and the Gate of Injury is at The Chasm. Those are assigned to Beidou and Yelan.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: As for the Gate of Terrain at Dihua Marsh, that's been taken by the Conqueror of Demons. These five are all on location already.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Today's the day Ningguang said to meet up again. Let's head to Yujing Terrace!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: We should head to Bubu Pharmacy first, or I won't catch them before they head out for Qingce Village.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where to next?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: To pay a visit to Yun Jin!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where should we go next?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: #I'll bet {NICKNAME}'s guessed it already. Hehe, to Wanmin Restaurant we go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, we've been to three places already... Is there anyone else you wanna give a coin to?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: But of course! Surely you didn't think I'd forgotten about you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! You got some for us, too?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Obviously! Come on, let's head to Wangsheng Funeral Parlor first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's already dark out... Should we go and head to the stage?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (She's not here... But these are her things...)

dialogues.speaker: Distant Voice
dialogues.text: Promise you won't stand us up this time?

dialogues.speaker: Distant Voice
dialogues.text: #Okay, I can get behind that... If you're a no-show, I'm sending {NICKNAME} to track you down and drag you back to the dinner table kicking and screaming!

dialogues.speaker: Distant Voice
dialogues.text: Nevertheless, I would urge caution. Focus on the task at hand, not what transpired in the past. And do not forget the rest of that saying: "Follow your heart, and do what you can."
